name: Peyton Mitchell
life: “I still remember reading a hospital leaflet to our sleeping cat.” Friday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Peyton takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I want to read to the shop cat first. It has yet to interrupt anybody's pronunciation.
appearance: Peyton is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a little coil of soft measuring tape, Peyton rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Peyton thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Peyton sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To read once to an undemanding listener.
family: Priya Tal is Peyton’s first cousin once removed. Peyton is free to hang up first. Priya makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The wrong bicycle*, Priya says, “My client had a receipt and no photograph. I found myself asking him for proof I'd never ask my neighbors for.”
connections: Lina Ryan. A tutor admits a deliberate reading mistake to the child practicing with the shop cat.

reactions.situation: A pupil chooses another language halfway through the reading
reactions.response: Peyton lets the pupil finish in the language they chose.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Peyton draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: When family demands an immediate answer
reactions.response: Peyton asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
